1.2.3.15-f98.text: Grammaticis olim & dialecticis Jurisque Professoribus, qui specimen eruditionis dedissent, eadem dignitatis insignia decreverunt Imperatores, quibus ornabant heroas

translations.note: The sidenote names a letter of Erasmus to Johannes Fabri, bishop of Vienna.

source.author: Erasmus
source.basis: sidenote "Erasm. ep. Jo. Fabio epis. Vien."
source.work: Letter to Johannes Fabri, bishop of Vienna

translations.text: Of old the emperors decreed to grammarians, dialecticians and professors of law who had given proof of their learning the same insignia of rank with which they adorned heroes

source.author: Philostratus; Lampridius
source.basis: text "as Philostratus relates of Hadrian and Lampridius of Alexander Severus"

1.2.3.15-f99.text: visu rerum, aut eruditione praestantes viri, mensis olim regum adhibit

translations.note: "visu rerum" is probably a corruption of "usu rerum" (experience of affairs). "adhibit" is cut short, presumably for "adhibiti" (admitted).

source.author: Philostratus; Lampridius
source.basis: text "as Philostratus relates of Hadrian and Lampridius of Alexander Severus"

translations.text: men eminent in experience of affairs or in learning were of old admitted to the tables of kings
